name: Reverse Seared, Butter-Basted Chuck Eye Steak
recipeDetails: A perfectly cooked chuck eye steak using the reverse sear method, finished with a butter baste for maximum flavor and tenderness. This technique ensures even cooking and a beautiful crust.
recipe:
### 1. Preparation
Remove the steak from the refrigerator and let it sit at room temperature for 30–60 minutes.
Pat the steak dry with paper towels. Season generously with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper.

### 2. Reverse Sear – Oven Cooking
Preheat your oven to 225°F (107°C).
Place the steak on a wire rack set over a rimmed baking sheet.
Insert an instant-read thermometer into the thickest part of the steak.
Cook in the oven until the internal temperature reaches 115°F (46°C) for medium-rare (30–45 minutes depending on thickness).

### 3. Searing and Butter Basting
Heat a cast-iron or heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat until very hot.
Add 1 tablespoon of neutral oil to the skillet.
Place the steak in the skillet and sear for about 45 seconds on one side.
Flip the steak and add butter, smashed garlic, and herbs.
Tilt the pan and spoon the melted butter over the steak for about 45 seconds.
Briefly sear the edges for a uniform crust.

### 4. Final Temperature and Serving
Ensure internal temperature is 125–130°F (52–54°C) for medium-rare.
Optionally rest the steak briefly on a cutting board.
Slice against the grain and serve immediately.
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon neutral oil (e.g., canola or avocado)
notes:
Dry steak surface before searing to improve crust.
Use a wire rack to promote even oven cooking.
Butter basting adds flavor and enhances browning.
While the overall recipe was 4.2/5, this was due to the low quality of the meat. With better meat this could have been 5/5.
